questions.question: What is Self-Refine's average improvement across 7 tasks in the original paper?
options: +5 absolute
+10 absolute
+20 absolute
+35 absolute
questions.explanation: Self-Refine (Madaan et al., NeurIPS 2023) achieves +20 absolute improvement averaged across 7 tasks (math, code, acronym, dialog) including GPT-4, with no training and no external tools.

questions.question: What is CRITIC's key improvement over Self-Refine?
options: CRITIC uses a larger model for critique
CRITIC routes the verification step through external tools like search engines, code interpreters, and test runners
CRITIC requires multiple critique rounds while Self-Refine uses one
CRITIC uses a separate model family for generation and critique
questions.explanation: CRITIC (Gou et al., arXiv:2305.11738) replaces Self-Refine's LLM self-feedback with tool-grounded verification — using search engines for facts, code interpreters for code, calculators for math — producing more reliable critiques.

questions.question: Why does Self-Refine require the refine prompt to include full history?
options: To save tokens by not recomputing the context
Because dropping prior outputs and critiques causes quality to drop sharply
To satisfy API requirements for multi-turn conversations
To enable the model to learn from positive examples
questions.explanation: The refine step in Self-Refine takes all prior outputs and critiques as context. The paper ablates this: dropping history causes quality to drop sharply because the model repeats previous mistakes without knowing what it already tried.

questions.question: What is the 'rubber-stamp loop' failure mode in self-refine systems?
options: The model generates the same output regardless of the critique
Same-prompt critique from the same model converges on 'looks good to me' without real improvement
The model applies feedback from the wrong task to the current task
The critique loop runs indefinitely without reaching convergence
questions.explanation: When the same model critiques its own output with the same prompt style, it tends to approve its own work ('looks good to me'). Fix with structurally different prompts or a different model for critique.

questions.question: How does Anthropic's 'evaluator-optimizer' workflow pattern map to Self-Refine and CRITIC?
options: It is a completely different pattern with no relationship to Self-Refine or CRITIC
It is Self-Refine/CRITIC reframed: Evaluator scores + produces critique, Optimizer revises, loop until evaluator passes
It is only equivalent to CRITIC, not Self-Refine
It adds a third 'generator' component not present in Self-Refine
questions.explanation: Anthropic's evaluator-optimizer is Self-Refine/CRITIC in Anthropic's framing: two roles (evaluator who scores and critiques, optimizer who revises) loop until the evaluator passes. The key engineering detail is using substantially different prompts for each role.

questions.question: What is the recommended stop condition for a production Self-Refine/CRITIC loop?
options: Stop after exactly one iteration
Stop when the model says it is done
Verifier passes OR model says fine AND iterations >= 2 OR iterations >= max_iterations
Stop only when external tests pass
questions.explanation: The 2026 default combines multiple conditions: stop if the verifier passes OR the model says fine AND at least 2 iterations have run OR max iterations reached. Never use a single-condition stop.
